title: Quasi-affine quotient by the normalizer of a split torus
statement: Let $S$ be any scheme [def-pc-scheme], and let $G\to S$ be a smooth affine group scheme of finite presentation [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] [pqf-def-affine-morphism] [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. Here a group scheme over $S$ is a group object in schemes over $S$, with multiplication, identity and inverse satisfying the group identities; finite presentation means locally of finite presentation, quasi-compact and quasi-separated [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. Fix an integer $r\geq0$ and a closed subgroup $T\hookrightarrow G$ [def-weil-closed-immersion] identified with $\mathbf G_{m,S}^r$, where $\mathbf G_m(W)=\Gamma(W,\mathcal O_W)^\times$ [def-sfb-relative-torus]. For an $S$-scheme $W$, put $G(W)=\operatorname{Hom}_S(W,G)$ and define $N(W)$ to be the subgroup of elements $g\in G(W)$ such that conjugation by $g$ preserves $T_W=T\times_SW$ as a subgroup functor, meaning $g_{W'}T(W')g_{W'}^{-1}=T(W')$ for every $W$-scheme $W'$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. Form the fppf sheafification of the presheaf of right coset sets $W\mapsto G(W)/N(W)$ [def-pc-fppf-site] [def-weil-pbc-sheafification]. This sheaf is represented by an $S$-scheme $X$ whose structure morphism $X\to S$ is smooth and quasi-affine [def-nagata-quasi-affine-morphism]. The canonical morphism $G\to X$ is a smooth surjection [def-weil-surjective-morphism]. No maximality assumption on $T$, reductivity or connectedness assumption on $G$, or Noetherian assumption on $S$ is imposed.

source.place: Theorem 2.3.1, printed pp.67-71, normalizer-quotient assertion specialized to a split torus; smoothness of the quotient map is stated in Remark 2.3.5, printed p.71, using Proposition 2.1.2. Read online; WANTED locally as literature/conrad-reductive-group-schemes.pdf. No Stacks tag states this relative group-scheme structural result.

proof.text: Fix any affine open $U=\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq S$; all objects in steps 1--7 are restricted to $U$. Smoothness and finite presentation of $G_U\to U$ persist by [lem-sfb-space-smooth-surjective-fppf-locality] and [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence](3), and $T_U\hookrightarrow G_U$ is closed by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change]. Apply [lem-sfb-relative-torus-centralizer-normalizer] to $T_U\hookrightarrow G_U$: the functor $N=N_{G_U}(T_U)$ is represented by a smooth affine finitely presented subgroup scheme, closed in $G_U$. Apply [lem-sfb-split-torus-finite-torsion-normalizer-detection] to choose $n\geq1$ with $N_{G_U}(T_U)=N_{G_U}(H)$ on all test schemes, where $H=T_U[n]=D_A((\mathbf Z/n\mathbf Z)^r)$. The displayed Laurent quotient in that node identifies $H$ with this finite diagonalizable group, including when $n$ is not invertible.

source.place: Theorem 2.3.1 proof, printed p.68, first paragraph; Proposition 2.1.2.

proof.text: Let $N$ act on $G_U$ on the left by $a\cdot g=ga^{-1}$. This action is free and its orbit sets are the right coset sets $G_U(W)/N(W)$. By [lem-pc-smooth-flat], smoothness of $N\to U$ implies flatness and local finite presentation. Apply [lem-sfb-free-flat-group-space-quotient] with $B=U$ to obtain the algebraic space $F=G_U/N$. Its map $q:G_U\to F$ is surjective, flat and locally finitely presented, has fppf-local sections on every scheme test, and $N\times_U G_U\simeq G_U\times_FG_U$ by $(a,g)\mapsto(ga^{-1},g)$. In particular the quotient is the fppf sheafification required in the statement.

source.place: Tag 06PH, lemma-quotient-free-action; application to right translation by a smooth closed subgroup.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-finite-diagonalizable-subgroup-parameter] to $H\hookrightarrow G_U$, obtaining $Y=Y_H$. Conjugation defines $G_U\to Y$, sending $g$ to $gH_Wg^{-1}$ on a test $W$. This is unchanged by $g\mapsto ga^{-1}$ with $a\in N(W)$, and $h_Y$ is an fppf sheaf [def-trf-scheme-algebraic-space], so the universal property of sheafification [def-weil-pbc-sheafification] gives $j:F\to Y$. This is monic: two sections of $F(W)$ have lifts $g,h$ on a common fppf cover by step 2. Equality of their images means $gH g^{-1}=hH h^{-1}$ there, hence $h^{-1}g\in N_{G_U}(H)=N$. Thus their right cosets agree on the cover, and the two sections agree because $F$ is a sheaf. This argument concerns subgroup functors on all tests, not merely geometric points.

source.place: Theorem 2.3.1 proof, printed pp.70-71, orbit map into the finite subgroup parameter scheme.

proof.text: The composite $j q:G_U\to Y$ is locally of finite type by [lemma-nagata-finite-type-to-separated-target](a), since $G_U\to U$ is of finite presentation. Apply [lem-sfb-representable-lft-fppf-source-descent] to $q$ and $j$, regarding algebraic spaces as stacks with only identity automorphisms: $q$ is surjective flat locally finitely presented by step 2, so $j$ is locally of finite type on etale charts. By [lem-sfb-space-lft-monomorphism-separated-lqf], $j$ is separated and chartwise locally quasi-finite. Its target $Y$ is a scheme, so [lem-a1-separated-locally-qf-space-representable] represents $F$ by a scheme $X_U$, with $j:X_U\to Y$ separated and locally quasi-finite.

source.place: Theorem 2.3.1 proof, printed pp.70-71; Tags 06EW, 0463 and 03XX.

proof.text: The map $q:G_U\to X_U$ is surjective on scheme points. Therefore $X_U$ is quasi-compact: pull back an open cover to the affine scheme $G_U$, choose a finite subcover there, and use surjectivity. By [lem-a1-lft-flat-lfp-source-descent], $X_U\to U$ is locally of finite type, hence of finite type. Since $U$ is affine, $Y$ is a quasi-affine scheme. The statement of [lem-trf-quasi-affine-canonical-affine-embedding] makes $Y$ separated; its relative diagonal over $U$ is the pullback of its absolute diagonal, so [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change] makes $Y\to U$ separated. Apply [lemma-nagata-finite-type-to-separated-target](b) to $X_U\to Y\to U$: $j$ is of finite type, in particular quasi-compact. Now all hypotheses of [lemma-nagata-zmt-quasi-affine-source] hold for $j$, and $X_U$ is quasi-affine.

source.place: Theorem 2.3.1 proof, printed pp.70-71, the Zariski Main Theorem step; Tags 02KL, 01P9, 01T8 and 0BCK.

proof.text: The scheme map $q:G_U\to X_U$ is an fppf cover by step 2 and [def-pc-fppf-site]. After base change along this very cover it is the projection $G_U\times_FG_U\simeq N\times_U G_U\to G_U$, up to interchanging the two factors of the kernel pair. This projection is smooth by base change of the smooth map $N\to U$. Hence [lem-sfb-space-smooth-surjective-fppf-locality] proves that $q$ is smooth. Since $q$ is flat, surjective and locally finitely presented and its composite with $X_U\to U$ is the given smooth map $G_U\to U$, [lem-sbc-smooth-flat-surjective-source-descent] proves $X_U\to U$ smooth. Surjectivity of $q$ is already part of step 2.

source.place: Proposition 2.1.2 and Theorem 2.3.1; quotient-map smoothness by Tags 0429, 03ZE, and base smoothness by Tag 05B5.

proof.text: For affine opens $V\subseteq U\subseteq S$, restriction of the quotient sheaf to $V$ is the fppf quotient $G_V/N_V$: the same local representatives and right-coset equalities define both sheaves, and restriction retains the universal property of [def-weil-pbc-sheafification]. Consequently $X_V$ is canonically isomorphic to $X_U\times_UV$, which is the open subscheme above $V$ by [lem-weil-pbc-open-fibre-product]. These canonical maps obey the identity and cocycle conditions because they identify the same quotient functors. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-relative-glueing-affine-opens] to all affine opens of $S$, producing $X\to S$ with inverse image $X_U$ over each $U$. The isomorphisms with the original quotient sheaf agree on the affine basis; they glue uniquely by the sheaf axiom, so $X$ represents that sheaf on every $S$-scheme.

For every affine open $U\subseteq S$, the inverse image $X_U$ is quasi-affine by step 5. Thus $X\to S$ is quasi-affine by [def-nagata-quasi-affine-morphism]. Open coverings are fppf coverings: their inclusions are etale by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation](1), hence flat locally finitely presented by [def-weil-etale-morphism]. Apply [lem-sfb-space-smooth-surjective-fppf-locality] to the covers $\{U\to S\}$ and $\{X_U\to X\}$ and step 6. It gives smoothness of $X\to S$ and smoothness and surjectivity of the glued canonical map $G\to X$. When $S$ is empty the same construction gives the empty scheme and all conclusions hold.
